oewn-02328781-a.learner: having more strength or power than is usual or than you would expect.
examples: Everything nourishes what is strong already.
With no expectation of pleasure, but with the strongest curiosity, Elizabeth opened the letter.

oewn-01517595-s.learner: not weak or hard to notice.
examples: With a stronger voice she soon added, "I have this comfort immediately"
There was a strong smell of smoke in the hall.

oewn-01832697-s.learner: having force or authority, or using it.
examples: The country was ruled by a strong king who was obeyed everywhere.

oewn-13984260-n.learner: the state of not being there.
examples: she was selected from among her sisters as worthy of being the mistress of Hunsford Parsonage, in the absence of more eligible visitors
There were better sense in the sad mechanic exercise of determining the reason of its absence where it is not.

oewn-15295848-n.learner: the length of time during which someone or something is away.
examples: After the first fortnight or three weeks of her absence, health, good-humour, and cheerfulness began to reappear at Longbourn.
though my absence may not be long enough to render it necessary

oewn-01236910-n.learner: not being present when you should be.
examples: he sometimes returned to Longbourn only in time to make an apology for his absence before the family went to bed

oewn-07590167-n.learner: the first meal of the day, which people usually eat in the morning.
examples: When breakfast was over, they were joined by the sisters
Mr. Gardiner left them soon after breakfast.

oewn-05827597-n.learner: a fact that has been checked and shown to be so.
examples: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife.
as a rational creature speaking the truth from her heart
He wrote down a few plain truths about the business.

oewn-13979774-n.learner: the state of agreeing with what is really so.
examples: Philosophers have argued for centuries about the nature of truth.

oewn-00818972-v.learner: to say that something is true, or to admit that it is real or that it exists.
examples: Georgiana, unable to support the idea of grieving and offending a brother, acknowledged the whole to me.
But why should you wish to persuade me that I feel more than I acknowledge?

oewn-01060995-v.learner: to show that you have noticed someone or something is there, or that you know them.
examples: He acknowledged her with a small bow as she passed him in the doorway.

oewn-00893988-v.learner: to say that you owe something to someone, or to thank them for it.
examples: Ever since I have known it I have been most anxious to acknowledge to you how gratefully I feel it.

oewn-02101619-v.learner: to put someone or something into a state or an activity quickly, suddenly, or without care.
examples: The very mention of anything concerning the match threw her into an agony of ill-humour.
The contents of this letter threw Elizabeth into a flutter of spirits.

oewn-01069686-v.learner: to say something with great force.
examples: He threw a curse at the driver and walked away.

connotation.why: casts the speaking as an act of attack

oewn-01511000-v.learner: to send something flying through the air.
examples: The boys threw stones into the river.

oewn-06646883-n.learner: a message that someone receives and understands.
examples: This information made Elizabeth smile, as she thought of poor Miss Bingley.
She resolved to give her the information herself

oewn-05824413-n.learner: knowledge that you get from study, from experience, or from being taught.
examples: She was a woman of mean understanding, little information, and uncertain temper.

oewn-08479331-n.learner: a set of facts that you can use to work something out.
examples: The scientists collected information from every station along the coast.

oewn-00710367-v.learner: to have something in your mind as the thing you mean to do.
examples: He had always intended to visit him, though to the last always assuring his wife that he should not go

oewn-00711208-v.learner: to plan or set something apart for a particular use or person.
examples: The money was intended for her education.

oewn-00957180-v.learner: to have a certain meaning in mind in what you say.
examples: What did you intend by that remark?

oewn-00029677-n.learner: something that happens at a particular place and time.
examples: This, madam, is a faithful narrative of every event in which we have been concerned together.

oewn-11430739-n.learner: something that comes after another thing and is caused by it.

oewn-00012993-r.learner: used to show that something is very likely.
